purpose: Assess sealed-bid target reliability with disjoint action-selection/evaluation worlds under neural population and exact search opponents. No gradients or strength qualification.
selection: Reuse all ten outcome-independently selected training roots from the runtime pilot, unchanged options. Do not select roots/actions using four-world pilot outcomes.
sample_semantics: The frozen sampler seeds each world by public_seed(root) plus sample index, independently of samples. Same numbered worlds paired across actions/populations; halves contain disjoint seed indices, each balanced over four population modes.
selection_rule: Choose max mean terminal credit only if its advantage over parent exceeds 1/40; favour parent on ties, otherwise smallest legal index. Fixed before new outcomes.
analysis: Both cross-fit directions: choose on 4..31, evaluate 32..59; choose on 32..59, evaluate 4..31. Select under neural_population, reference_opponent_v1 and their equal-weight mixture; report each on both held-out populations. Average directions within root, equal weight roots. Report all roots, overrides, sign disagreements and selection optimism. Do not tune threshold on evaluation halves.
limitations: Only ten training roots, one per count/rules stratum. Cross-fit directions share roots and are not independent observations. Conditional terminal credit is not a game win-rate gain. Opponent identity is a diagnostic intervention, not a policy feature. No model selected; broader whole-deal-heldout data needed before training/promotion.
estimate_basis: Four-world pilot time times 14, LPT partition on runtime only. Two four-worker lanes; extrapolation, not measured concurrent throughput.
failure: Stop both lanes on first cap/failure or at twelve hours; preserve all raw/partial output. No automatic retries or follow-on jobs.
next_gate: Independent raw audit, then examine repeatability and cross-population transfer on all roots. No four-world pilot labels admitted. Decide a broader target/learning experiment before HF training.
